title: Sharada Tilaka Tantra (Laxmanacharya)
shelf_note: Lakṣmaṇadeśika's Śāradātilaka, a core Śākta-Tantric ritual manual; belongs on a Hindu/Sanskrit shelf. The catalogue date 1100 is the work's date, not this printed edition's.
structure_note: 291 leaves, all with OCR and translation. The 59 backsteps and 69 repeats in printed numbers are most likely misread page tags, not a broken scan: leaf 222 is printed 219 but the OCR tags it 214, and leaf 150 is tagged 149. The four sampled leaves run in order (printed 42, 135, ~147, 219).

book_verdict: The right text on the right leaves. The OCR is mostly sound but slips on rarer words, and the lite-model translation then reads smoothly over those misreads. On two of four pages that changes the meaning, including an encoded mantra rendered wrongly.
reader_summary: This is a printed Devanagari text of the Śāradātilaka, Lakṣmaṇadeśika's Tantric ritual manual, and the transcription is of that text, leaf by leaf. The English follows the verses in order and is usable for ritual sequence. Where the OCR misreads a word it does not flag it: mantra encodings and the effects of rites are sometimes wrong (on p.135 'brings him under control' becomes 'makes the invisible visible'), so check any technical verse against the Devanagari.

title: Tantraloka Vol. 1 with Jayaratha Commentary
shelf_note: Abhinavagupta's Tantrāloka with Jayaratha's Viveka, KSTS 1918; a central work of Kashmir Śaivism.
structure_note: Two printed paginations in one scan. Leaves 36, 51 and 211 run printed 26 (on verse 7), 41 (verse 18) and 201 (verse 166). Near the end, leaf 340 is printed 18 (verses 21–22) and leaf 348 is printed 26 (verses 31–32). This is a second run of printed pages 1–40-odd covering the opening of Āhnika 1, but its text and verse positions differ from the first run's. It looks like a spliced-in section (another printing, or a supplement) placed after the main text, which explains the 73 printed repeats. It needs checking against the IA item. 4 leaves have no OCR and 13 are untranslated.

book_verdict: The strongest book in this packet: accurate Devanagari, faithful English that keeps the variant-reading apparatus. The defects are cosmetic (model meta and summary blocks, tag leaks) plus a structural question about a second pagination run near the end of the scan.
reader_summary: This is the 1918 Kashmir Series edition of Tantrāloka Āhnika 1 with Jayaratha's commentary, transcribed accurately, footnoted variant readings included. The English is a faithful, readable rendering of verse and commentary and can be trusted for the argument. It is wrapped in model-written preface and summary boxes, which are not part of the text. The last ~40 leaves restart the printed pagination and should not be cited until that section is identified.

title: Paramesvaratantra
shelf_note: The Cambridge palm-leaf Parameśvaratantra (dated 828 CE in the catalogue), an early Śaiva tantra; right tradition. The collections field is empty.
structure_note: 124 leaves, but only 52 have a printed number, and that number is the transcriber's guess. The OCR tags leaf 62 as page '3' while a pencil foliation '31' is visible on it. Leaf 80 is tagged 41, but the leaf carries '40'. The 23 backsteps come from these guessed leaf numbers, not from a disordered scan. The leaves seem to run in order (leaf 112 carries '56').

book_verdict: A precious early Nepalese palm-leaf manuscript that the flash model cannot read. The transcriptions are partly confabulated or looping, and the English builds fluent ritual content, headings and 'syllables' out of the garble. The OCR even dates the leaf to the 17th–18th century.
reader_summary: The images are the Cambridge palm-leaf manuscript of the Parameśvaratantra, an early Śaiva tantra in an early Nepalese hand. The transcription is not a reliable reading of it: a few words match the leaf, and much of the rest is invented or repeated. The English should not be trusted at all; it turns misread letters into mantras, stories and notes.

title: Rig-Veda-Sanhita: Sacred Hymns of the Brahmans (Vol. 3)
shelf_note: Max Müller's edition of the Ṛgveda with Sāyaṇa's commentary, Vol. III (Maṇḍalas 5–7 on the sampled pages). Published is given as 1849, which is Vol. I's date; Vol. III is later (1856, or the 1890–92 second edition).
structure_note: 1062 leaves. The 101 backsteps and 134 repeats are most likely from the OCR's page tags: several leaves carry two numbers (aṣṭaka/varga and page), and blank leaves are tagged 'None'. The sampled leaves run in order (blank, 309, 623, 922). 4 leaves have no OCR and 13 are untranslated.

book_verdict: A sound transcription of a standard Vedic edition, with saṃhitā, padapāṭha and Sāyaṇa's commentary kept in order. The English is mostly reliable but sometimes reverses a word: on p.922 a mantra's 'unwise' becomes 'wise'.
reader_summary: This is Max Müller's printed Ṛgveda with Sāyaṇa's commentary (Vol. III). The transcription is the right text and accurate to the line, with accents converted to Unicode marks. The English translates hymn, word-by-word analysis and commentary, and is generally faithful. It occasionally inverts or substitutes a gloss, so check the hymn line against the Sanskrit before quoting it.
